source_text: Fecit distinctionem, ne quis putaret transisse peccatum, ut mors, quae praecucurrit, iudicante iustitia secuta probaretur materias ultionis, quas in unoquoque peccatore de studio malae voluntatis invenerat. Ostendit igitur non naturam accusandam esse, sed studia.
pass_a_gloss: He made a distinction, lest anyone think that sin passed, so that death, which ran ahead, with justice judging, would be proved to have followed the materials of vengeance which it had found in each sinner from a pursuit of an evil will. He showed therefore that not nature is to be accused, but pursuits.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: He made a distinction so that no one would think sin had passed on. Death, which had gone before, was shown under justice’s judgment to follow grounds for punishment which it found in each sinner’s pursuit of an evil will. He therefore showed that nature must not be accused, but deliberate conduct.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
